**Summary: Comparison of Crowdworker vs. NLP Toolkits for Political Tweet Analysis (NER & ELS)**

This study evaluates the accuracy of **crowdworkers** versus **seven NLP toolkits** in performing two critical NLP tasks — **Named Entity Recognition (NER)** and **Entity-Level Sentiment (ELS) Analysis** — on a challenging dataset of **1,000 political tweets** collected during the **U.S. presidential primary election in February 2016**. Each tweet references at least one of four candidates: **Bernie Sanders, Donald Trump, Hillary Clinton, and Ted Cruz**. Groundtruth labels were established by **experts in political communication**, and crowdworkers (hired via Amazon Mechanical Turk) were also used for annotation, with the latter’s performance serving as a benchmark. ---

### **Dataset & Annotation Methodology**

- **Dataset**: 1,000 tweets, heavily skewed toward **Trump** (more than twice as many tweets about him as others). - **Groundtruth**: Provided by political communication experts. - **Crowdworker Annotation**: Based on a **decision tree model** that assigns 2–7 workers per tweet depending on:
  - Tweet length
  - Presence of links
  - Sarcasm signals (which increase disagreement and task difficulty)
- **Sentiment Labels**: 3-class system: **positive, neutral, negative**. - **NER Labels**: Identifies which candidate (entity) is mentioned in each tweet. ---

### **NLP Toolkits Evaluated**

#### **Named Entity Recognition (NER) Tools**:
1. **Google Cloud NL** (most accurate NER system tested)
2. **TwitterNLP** (default settings)
3. **Stanford NLP NER** (3-class: person, organization, location — higher accuracy than 7-class)
4. **CogComp-NLP** (using Ontonotes 5.0 model)
5. **spaCy** (using `en_core_web_lg` model)

#### **Entity-Level Sentiment (ELS) Tools**:
1. **Rosette Text Analytics**
2. **Google Cloud NL**
3. **TensiStrength** (most accurate ELS system tested)
4. **TwitterNLP**
5. **CogComp-NLP**
6. **Stanford NLP NER** (used for sentiment analysis in some cases)
7. **Google Cloud NL** (also used for ELS)

> Note: **TensiStrength** and **Rosette** are rule-based sentiment tools using dictionaries and sentiment rules. **Google Cloud NL** and **Rosette** are commercial APIs; **TensiStrength** is open-source. ---

### **Performance Metrics**

- **Correct Classification Rate (CCR)**: Used for both tasks. - **NER**: Number of correctly identified entities (candidates) per tweet. - **ELS**: Number of correctly predicted sentiment labels (positive/neutral/negative) per candidate mention. ---

### **Key Results**

#### **Named Entity Recognition (NER)**

- **Crowdworkers**: Achieved **98.6% CCR** — near-perfect accuracy. - **Automated Systems**:
  - **Google Cloud NL**: 96.7% CCR — **almost on par with crowdworkers**. - **spaCy**: 77.2%–91% CCR, but **struggled with “Trump”** (only 72.7% accuracy). - **TwitterNLP**: ~80% CCR. - **Stanford NER**: ~85% CCR. - **CogComp-NLP**: ~80% CCR. > **Observation**: NER performance was generally high, with **Google Cloud NL** being the most accurate. However, **Trump** was consistently harder to identify across systems, likely due to his frequent mentions and varied phrasing. #### **Entity-Level Sentiment (ELS) Analysis**

- **Crowdworkers**: **74.7% CCR** — significantly higher than any NLP tool. - **Automated Systems**:
  - **Rosette Text Analytics**: 31.7% CCR — lowest performance. - **Google Cloud NL**: 43.2% CCR — poor at identifying **positive** and **negative** sentiments (only 3% and 19%, respectively). - **TensiStrength**: 44.2% CCR — **still 30+ percentage points below crowdworkers**. - **TwitterNLP**: Not reported in detail, but likely low. - **CogComp-NLP**: Not reported in detail, but likely low. > **Breakdown by Sentiment Class**:
- **Crowdworkers**:
  - 62% neutral
  - 85% positive
  - 92% negative
- **Google Cloud NL**:
  - 88% neutral
  - 3% positive
  - 19% negative
- **TensiStrength**:
  - 87.2% neutral
  - 10.5% positive
  - 8.1% negative
- **Rosette**:
  - 22.7% neutral
  - 38.1% negative
  - 40.9% positive

> **Observation**: **ELS is significantly harder** for NLP tools. Even the best system (**TensiStrength**) underperformed crowdworkers by **>30 percentage points**. Crowdworkers were especially accurate at identifying **negative** sentiment (92%), while tools struggled with **positive** and **negative** sentiment. ---

### **Key Challenges & Insights**

1. **Political tweets are inherently difficult** due to:
   - **Sarcasm** and **irony** (causes disagreement among crowdworkers and confuses NLP tools).
